pa_maple_wall.blurb: Maple Wall is a steep sandstone crag above the Youghiogheny bike trail in Ohiopyle State Park. The main face bulges and overhangs, reaching roughly 90 feet, with the gentler lines toward the left and the tougher ones on the right. Of its ten climbs, most are bolted, with a couple of trad lines and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.7 and climb to the low 5.12s, so there is a handful of moderates for warming up and a few hard, powerful routes for strong climbers. It is less conspicuous from the trail than the neighboring School House Wall, and the rock is best suited to people comfortable on overhanging ground.
pa_maple_wall.approach: From the bike trail just past the white mile marker 76, a path leaves on the left opposite a bench and pulloff. Look for a big black boulder and a sign reading 76 Maple Wall; the wall is a few minutes through the woods.

pa_creekside_the_split_boulders.blurb: A small trailside cluster within the Governor Stable boulder field in south-central Pennsylvania, made of diabase. Ten problems are spread over two groups: the Creekside boulder, which holds the best lines, and the Split boulders, which are decent but less notable. Difficulty runs from the easiest grades up to V7, with a few mid-range V2 to V4 problems that make it a worthwhile stop for most climbers, and a couple of hard traverse and throw lines for the strong. Bring a pad and a spotter, since some landings are tight. The walk in from the warm-up boulders takes only about five minutes.
pa_creekside_the_split_boulders.approach: Follow the main trail from the warm-up boulders for about five minutes, then take the small side trail that bends left around a large boulder toward the creek.

pa_kelly_drive_boulder.blurb: A single city boulder in Philadelphia, tucked between Kelly Drive and the busy Schuylkill River Trail bike path. It holds ten problems, most of them easy to moderate: a couple of V0 and V1 lines and traverses, a cluster around V2, one V3, and a few harder problems up to V5 for those wanting a challenge. It has a reputation as a pleasant place to work easy problems while it is sunny. Expect passing cyclists and runners, and bring a crash pad, since this is a short urban session rather than a day out.

pa_3_battlements.blurb: Battlements is a trad-focused cliff in Susquehanna Riverlands State Park, in York County above the river. Ten routes run roughly 50 to 60 feet, from 5.5 up to 5.9, so it suits newer leaders as well as those seeking a moderate tick list. The quartzite here has seen little traffic, so expect some loose rock; a helmet is wise, and it helps to inspect a line on top rope before leading it. A climbers' path follows the base of the cliffs, and plenty of trees along the top allow a rappel back down or a walk around the side.
